findings.evidence: D7 says every Compose command other than `pnpm stack:up` and the bare README command passes `--no-build` and `--pull never` to `up`, and `--pull never` to `run`, "so a missing image fails the command". Compose's `--pull` flag overrides pull_policy for every service, so it also stops `db` (postgres:16.16-bookworm) and `caddy` (caddy:2.11.9-alpine) from being pulled. Nothing pulls them first: the CI `image` job only runs `pnpm ci:image` (FROM node) and `pnpm test:infra`, and it has no Postgres service container. `compose-config.test.ts` runs `config`, which pulls nothing. The only possible pull is `media.test.ts` starting its throwaway Caddy with `docker run`, and that races with the parallel files. So `docker compose -p jade-infra-... up -d --wait --no-build --pull never` in compose-up, caddy-logs and media fails with "No such image" on the first CI run, on a clean dev machine (Caddy was never pulled; Postgres only if devdb ran) and in clean-clone setups. AC8 and the required `image` job therefore go red for a reason unrelated to the code. Z4b has the same gap: it pulls only the app reference, so the first deploy on a VM built from `deploy/staging/` fails, and so does any later deploy that bumps the pinned db or caddy tag (jade-8ho digest pinning).
findings.fix: Limit the no-pull rule to the app image. Either set `pull_policy: never` (with `--no-build`) on `app` and `migrate` in compose.prod.yml and drop the global `--pull never` flag, or keep the flag and add a step that pulls the pinned third-party images first (`docker compose -p <project> -f compose.prod.yml pull db caddy`). That step goes in the infra tests' shared setup, the deploy script and the rehearsal, before any `up` or `run`. Make compose-config/ci-workflow tests assert the chosen form, and run compose-up in a check that starts with no caddy image (for example, it removes the pinned caddy tag first, or CI's fresh runner shows it).

findings.evidence: PD14 rests on the one daemon-wide tag `jade-app:ci`, which `pnpm test:infra` rebuilds in whichever checkout runs it. PD13 accepts that two checkouts or bugfix worktrees share one Docker daemon. Suppose test:infra in checkout B rebuilds `jade-app:ci` after A's build and before A's stack comes up. A's compose-up then runs B's image, and its ID check still passes, because the container and the tag are both B's at that moment. A's AC8 evidence, recorded in bead notes while no CI exists, would prove other code. PD11 calls exactly this a passing check against another process and rules it out. `jade-app:local`, used by `pnpm stack:up`, is shared the same way.
findings.fix: Tag the image per checkout and run, for example `jade-app:ci-<checkout hash>-<run id>`, using the hash `tools/compose.ts` already derives. `test:infra` exports it as `JADE_IMAGE` to every infra test, and CI pushes the tag its own run built. Use `jade-app:local-<checkout hash>` for `pnpm stack:up` too. compose-up keeps comparing the container's image ID with the ID `image.test.ts` checked, taken from that per-run tag.

findings.evidence: Since revision 3, compose-up, caddy-logs and media run the prebuilt `jade-app:ci` with `--no-build`. No automated check now runs the `build:` stanza that `pnpm stack:up` and the bare `docker compose -f compose.prod.yml up` of OB13 depend on. A wrong build context, a missing `APP_VERSION` argument or a stanza on only one of `app`/`migrate` would pass AC8 while the README command fails. The image build is also defined twice: section 11 says `pnpm test:infra` "builds `jade-app:ci` first", yet the CI `image` job runs `pnpm ci:image` and then `pnpm test:infra`. The changelog says the budget stands because "the image job no longer builds a second image", but the plan never says whether test:infra builds through `ci:image` on the same buildx builder, or how. A plain build on the default builder would add up to the 3:00 cold build to a 6:15 job with a 9-minute timeout.
findings.fix: Keep one build definition. Make `pnpm ci:image` build through compose.prod.yml's own stanza (`JADE_IMAGE=<tag> docker compose -f compose.prod.yml build app`, or bake from it), or have compose-config assert that the stanza matches the arguments `ci:image` passes. State that `test:infra` builds only by calling `pnpm ci:image`, on the same builder, and that the CI job's explicit `ci:image` step is either dropped or a cache hit. Have ci-workflow.test.ts assert this, and restate the 12.2 row if the second build is counted.
